newsitem.title: LEBANON: Second Iraqi group claims Uday assassination bid.
newsitem.headline: Second Iraqi group claims Uday assassination bid.

text.p: A previously unknown Iraqi opposition group claimed responsibility on Saturday for the assassination attempt on President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday.

"The Iraq Salvation Movement is the group behind the attack on Uday," a man told an international news agency in Beirut by telephone. It was the second group to claim of responsibility for the Thursday attack in Baghdad.
"Our information says the attack may have led to his death or severe injury as one of the attackers who returned safely saw blood covering Uday's face," said the man who spoke in Arabic.
The caller said the Iraq Salvation Movement was a front that included several small opposition groups working inside Iraq.
The Tehran-based Iraqi opposition group, the Islamic Dawa Party, said on Friday it was behind the attempt.
Uday's car was attacked by gunmen as he drove unguarded on Thursday evening in Baghdad's smart al-Mansour disctrict.
Witnesses said at least two gunmen carried out the attack, wounding 32-year-old Uday and several bystanders. Uday was reported to be in a Baghdad hospital but without serious wounds.
